facts_known: Complainant: B-04-02, Block B, floor 4, occupied by a tenant, 10 share units. Reported source unit: none (not applicable).
November bill shows charges RM 200 and sinking fund RM 12.
Late interest was charged on the October bill, which was paid 20 days late.
Complainant asks which sinking fund rate is right (friend says at least 10%) and asks about the late interest charged.
facts_missing: Date the October bill was due and the date the notice of that unpaid sum was received by the parcel (needed to apply By-law 6(1)(a): a defaulter is someone who has not paid at the expiry of 14 days after receiving a notice).
Date the October payment was actually received.
Amount of late interest charged and how it was calculated.
Whether the bills are addressed to the registered proprietor or to the tenant, and whether the tenant is the one paying (the complainant's role in the billing).

rules.quote: but such contribution to the sinking fund shall not be less than ten per cent of the charges.
rules.applies: Governs the sinking fund rate. The Act sets a floor of 10% of the charges. The RM 12 shown is 6% of RM 200, which is below this floor. A general meeting may set a different amount under s61(3), but not below 10%.

rules.quote: The contribution to the sinking fund is 6% of the charges.
rules.applies: Additional by-law 8(2) sets 6%. This conflicts with ACT-s61(3) and is overridden to the extent it is below 10%. Other parts of ABL-8 (charges RM 200 a month, monthly in advance, interest at 10% a year daily) are not in conflict and apply.

rules.quote: Interest on late payment is charged at 10% a year on a daily basis, as provided in by-law 6(2) of the Third Schedule.
rules.applies: Sets the late interest rate at 10% a year, charged daily, under by-law 6(2). Interest only arises under by-law 6 once the 14-day condition in BL-6(1)(a) is met, so whether this October interest was properly charged depends on the notice and payment dates still missing.

rules.quote: a defaulter is a proprietor who has not fully paid the Charges or contribution to the sinking fund in respect of his parcel or any other money imposed by or due and payable to the management corporation under the Act at the expiry of the period of fourteen days of receiving a notice from the management corporation
rules.applies: Defines when interest starts to run: only if the sum is still unpaid at the end of 14 days after a notice. Needs the notice date and payment date to check the interest charged.

rules.quote: the proprietor shall pay interest at the rate of ten per cent per annum on a daily basis or at such rate as shall be determined by the management corporation at a general meeting, until the date of actual payment of the sum due.
rules.applies: Same point: interest runs daily until actual payment, after the 14-day period. Rate is 10% a year unless a general meeting sets another rate within the Act's limit.

rules.quote: determine the amount of interest payable by a proprietor in respect of late payments which shall not exceed the rate of ten per cent per annum.
rules.applies: Confirms the Act caps late interest at 10% a year. The 10% in ABL-8(4) and BL-6(2) is within this cap.

conflict.governs: ACT-s61(3) of the Strata Management Act 2013 governs over ABL-8(2) of the Amber Residences Additional By-laws, under SOP-3 precedence (Act first, then Third Schedule, then additional by-laws).
conflict.why: The Act requires the sinking fund contribution to be not less than 10% of the charges. ABL-8(2) sets 6%. The Act prevails, so the sinking fund cannot be 6% of RM 200 (RM 12). On the RM 200 charge, the Act minimum is RM 20 a month. The Act is not in conflict with ABL-8(1), (3) or (4).

next_steps.action: Acknowledge the email within one working day, by email, using the acknowledge template.

Ask the complainant for the missing facts: the October bill due date, the date the notice was received, the date the October payment was made, and the interest amount billed. Confirm whether the bill is addressed to the proprietor or the tenant.

Check the November bill against ACT-s61(3): the sinking fund on RM 200 charges should be at least 10%, which is RM 20, not RM 12. Record that ABL-8(2) (6%) is overridden by the Act. Check the sinking fund billing history for the parcel, as the same 6% rate may have been applied in earlier months.

Check the October late interest against BL-6(1)(a) and BL-6(2) once the notice date and payment date are on file. Interest applies only if the sum was unpaid 14 days after notice, and only at 10% a year, daily, until payment.

Do not send any reminder or notice about the sinking fund or interest until the billing check is finished and the facts are verified. Any change to what was billed is for the office to decide through its usual billing process; do not promise a refund or a corrected amount to the resident.

rules.quote: a fine of RM 50 may be imposed for each breach of these additional by-laws or the Third Schedule by-laws for which no other fine is set.
rules.applies: This is the rule that answers the complainant's question on which rule allows a fine. The RM 50 amount was set by the general meeting of 15 March 2025. The fine is available only for a verified breach that is notified in writing, and only if the management corporation imposed it. Check the notice against ABL-9(2) before anyone treats the fine as settled.

rules.quote: A fine is imposed only by the management corporation after the breach has been verified and the person concerned has been notified in writing. Staff of the management office do not impose fines on their own.
rules.applies: The office must confirm that the notice of 10 November 2026 followed a verified breach and was issued by the management corporation. If the facts show it was issued by staff alone, that is a question the building manager must decide under penalty_not_authorised.

rules.quote: The management corporation may by a resolution at a general meeting impose a fine of such amount as shall be determined by that general meeting against any person who is in breach of any of these by-laws or any additional by-laws made under the Act.
rules.applies: Third Schedule by-law 7 gives the management corporation the power to fine by general meeting resolution. ABL-9 sets the amount under this power. The two are consistent, so there is no conflict to resolve.

rules.quote: imposition of fine not exceeding two hundred ringgit against any proprietor, occupant or invitee who is in breach of any of the by-laws.
rules.applies: Section 70(2)(i) of the Act sets the ceiling for an additional by-law fine at RM 200. The RM 50 fine under ABL-9 is within that ceiling. Section 70(2)(i) governs over ABL-9 on the amount, but the RM 50 amount is within it.
